sections.rawHeading: 1 · Licensing (GOV — high confidence; registration for most chimney work, plus one real hearth-install license)
sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; registration for most chimney work, plus one real hearth-install license
sections.markdown:
**Iowa's general contractor credential is a statewide REGISTRATION, not a competency license.** Under **Iowa Code Chapter 91C**, anyone "engage[d] in the business of construction" must register with the **Dept. of Inspections, Appeals & Licensing (DIAL)**; people earning **less than $2,000 a year** from construction, or working only on their own property, are excluded (§ 91C.1). DIAL charges a **$50 application fee**, and all registrants need an Iowa unemployment-insurance number. **Out-of-state contractors must file a $25,000 surety bond** (§ 91C.2), and DIAL says this applies to out-of-state contractors with employees; the bond secures **taxes and unemployment contributions**, not homeowners (§ 91C.7). **Registration tests no skill.** It is a labor and tax compliance filing. Lookup: start from DIAL's contractor-registration page (https://dial.iowa.gov/licenses/building/contractors), which links the public contractor search (laborportal.iwd.iowa.gov/iwd_portal/publicSearch/public — returned 404 to an automated fetch on Sep 25, 2026 but is still linked by DIAL's page updated 6/26/26; link the DIAL page, not the portal directly).

**The exception, and it matters for hearth work: the Hearth Systems Specialty License (STATE LAW).** Iowa's Plumbing and Mechanical Systems Board, administered by DIAL, issues a **Hearth Systems Specialty License**. Iowa Code § 105.18 lets the board issue special licenses for "a limited class or classes of plumbing or mechanical professional work." **Rules (RESOLVED Sep 25 2026): 481 IAC 429.2(10)** (application; NFI or board-approved certification) and **481 IAC 431.7** (scope; licensee "will maintain the person's valid certification issued from the National Fireplace Institute or equivalent authority approved by the board"), both effective 6/19/24 and transferred from 641—29.2 and 641—23.7 (https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/iac/rule/481.429.2.pdf ; https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/iac/rule/481.431.7.pdf).
- **Scope:** "installation of gas burning and solid fuel appliances that offer a decorative view of the flames, from the connector pipe to the shutoff valve located within 3 feet of the appliance," plus "venting systems, log lighters, gas log sets, fireplace inserts, and freestanding stoves."
- **Requirements:** age 18+, a completed application and fees, and **"a valid certification issued by the National Fireplace Institute [NFI] or equivalent authority approved by the board."**
- **What it does NOT cover:** chimney sweeping, chimney masonry, crowns or rebuilds.

So in Iowa, a **fireplace-insert, stove, or venting installer** works under a real trade license that requires an NFI certification. A **sweep or chimney mason** holds only the Ch. 91C registration. Local permit rules layer on top (LOCAL). **Cedar Rapids** issues no city contractor license of its own: "In order for contractors to perform work and be issued a permit in the City of Cedar Rapids, licensing with the State of Iowa is required," listing building, electrical and mechanical/plumbing contractors, with no masonry or chimney license (https://www.cedar-rapids.org/local_government/departments_a_-_f/building_services/building_and_trades/licensing_for_contractors.php). **Des Moines:** its Permit & Development Center's contractor material covers only state Ch. 91C registration; no city masonry/chimney license was found, but its municipal code was not read, so say "not confirmed" for Des Moines.

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: For sweeps and masons, the gap is as wide as it gets. The state credential is a **labor-compliance registration** that verifies UI and workers'-comp compliance, and says nothing about masonry or flue diagnosis. The one real test sits on **installation**: the Hearth Systems license requires NFI certification. Nothing tests **inspection or repair** judgment. Individual certifications (CSIA CCS, C-DET; NCSG CCP/CCR) and independent audits are the only competence signal for the diagnosis and upsell side of the trade.

sections.rawHeading: 3 · Home sale (GOV — high confidence; mandatory form but NO chimney line — re-confirmed on the 2026 form)
sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence; mandatory form but NO chimney line — re-confirmed on the 2026 form
sections.markdown:
**Iowa mandates seller disclosure under Iowa Code Chapter 558A, but the state form does NOT name chimney, fireplace, or flue.**
- **Delivery (§ 558A.2):** the transferor or their broker must deliver a written disclosure statement before a written offer is made or accepted.
- **Content (§ 558A.4):** statements cover property condition, including "significant defects in the structural integrity" and, since a 2025 amendment effective Jan 1, 2026, **lead service lines.** The Real Estate Commission sets the content by rule.
- **Where the rule lives now:** the old 193E—14.1 rule was **transferred to 481 IAC 2014.1** (IAC Supplement 6/10/26). The form is at **subrule 2014.1(7)** (history: ARC 0027D, effective 4/22/26).
- **What the form lists:** the current form has **20 numbered items**. Among them are Basement/Foundation, Roof, Heating System(s), Physical Problems and Structural Damage, plus a new **item 13: "Are there currently, or have there ever been, any lead water service lines present?"** **None names chimney, fireplace, flue or wood stove.** A chimney defect surfaces only under "Roof," "Heating System(s)," "Physical Problems," or "Structural Damage," on an actual-knowledge basis.

No inspection is mandated at transfer; NFPA 211 Level 2 stays a NATIONAL STANDARD.

sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.markdown:
Iowa gives consumers two tracks, plus a cancellation right:
- **(1) Iowa Consumer Fraud Act, § 714.16.** It bars deception, fraud, false promise, misrepresentation and concealment of material fact. **The AG enforces it.**
- **(2) Private right of action, Ch. 714H.** Consumers recover **actual damages** plus **costs and reasonable attorney's fees**. For conduct showing **"willful and wanton disregard for the rights or safety of another"**, proven "by a preponderance of clear, convincing, and satisfactory evidence," courts may award **statutory damages up to three times actual damages** (§ 714H.5). The deadline is two years from violation or discovery.
- **Door-to-door cancel.** The Door-to-Door Sales Act (Ch. 555A) gives a **3-business-day right to cancel** (notice form in § 555A.3), and a Ch. 555A violation is also a § 714.16 violation.

Complaints: iowaattorneygeneral.gov Consumer Protection Division.

sections.rawHeading: 5 · Permits & codes (GOV — high confidence on the state code; local adoption varies)
sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence on the state code; local adoption varies
sections.markdown:
The **Iowa State Building Code (Iowa Code Ch. 103A)** now adopts the **2024 IRC** (481 IAC 301.8) and **2024 IBC** (481 IAC 301.3), both **effective 9/10/25**. It governs buildings made subject to it by Ch. 103A, and projects under a local code follow local enforcement. **Most residential enforcement is LOCAL:**
- **Des Moines** adopted the **2024 IRC, effective Jan 1, 2026.**
- **Cedar Rapids** lists the **2024 IRC** as adopted.
- Rural areas may have limited or no residential enforcement.

Where a building department exists, chimney relines, rebuilds, crowns and solid-fuel appliance installs are generally permit work; routine sweeps and like-for-like caps generally are not.

sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.markdown: **Iowa Code § 10A.518** requires CO alarms in **existing single-family rentals and multiple-unit residential buildings**, and in **single-family and multi-unit construction begun on or after July 1, 2018**, wherever the dwelling has a **"fuel-fired heater or appliance, a fireplace, or an attached garage."** The statute names the **fireplace** as a trigger. For rentals, landlords must install alarms and fix inoperable ones **within 30 days of written notice**; placement follows rules set by the director. There is no statewide pre-sale CO certificate. A permitted chimney or solid-fuel job is the natural moment to verify alarms.

sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.markdown: No statewide burn-ban or stove-emission regime. Not a material content section for IA.

sections.title: Scam patterns and enforcement
sections.markdown: The Iowa AG's Consumer Protection Division publishes storm-chaser and home-repair scam warnings, plus annual top-10 complaint lists (iowaattorneygeneral.gov newsroom). A door-knock "we noticed your chimney" pitch is a textbook Ch. 555A + § 714.16 scenario. **No IA chimney-sweep-specific enforcement action has been confirmed.** Use patterns, not names.

sections.title: Season calendar
sections.markdown: Cold continental climate with harsh winters statewide. Burn season runs ~Oct–Apr. Rush: SEP–NOV. Best booking: APR–JUN.

sections.title: Price seeding (internal)
sections.markdown: Des Moines and the Cedar Rapids/Iowa City corridor run **near national**; rural counties run below national. Regionalize modestly; overall spread is low.

story.heading: The story
story.markdown:
Iowa's general "license" is a **paper registration**: a $50 labor-compliance filing under Ch. 91C that proves you pay workers'-comp, nothing about whether you can read a flue. But Iowa has one twist most states lack. **Installing a fireplace insert, wood stove or its venting takes a real state Hearth Systems Specialty License backed by an NFI certification**, while sweeping and inspecting a chimney takes nothing. The person who *diagnoses* your chimney is the least regulated person in the chain.

On the master-finding axis, Iowa **partially BREAKS the correlation**:
- As a weak-credential state it runs a genuinely mandatory disclosure (Ch. 558A), as the theory predicts.
- **But the form, revised again in 2026 to add lead service lines, still has no chimney, fireplace or flue line.**
- Its CO law (§ 10A.518) names the *fireplace* as a trigger, while the disclosure form ignores the chimney entirely.

The sharp content: check the hearth license for installs, get an independent inspection for everything else, and use the Ch. 714H treble-damages remedy if you're defrauded.

h1: Iowa chimney & fireplace laws: know your rights
metaDescription: Iowa chimney & fireplace laws: licensing, seller disclosure, right to cancel and CO alarm rules, with statutes cited.

season.note: Cold continental climate with harsh winters statewide. Burn season runs ~Oct–Apr. Rush: SEP–NOV. Best booking: APR–JUN.

faq.q: What should I check before hiring a chimney company in Iowa?
faq.a: State licensing: Mostly NO — Ch. 91C REGISTRATION for sweeps/masons ($2k/yr threshold, DIAL); BUT hearth appliance/insert/stove/venting installs need the state Hearth Systems Specialty License (NFI certification; Plumbing & Mechanical Systems Board under Ch. 105; 481 IAC 429.2(10), 431.7). Registration or credential: YES — Ch. 91C contractor registration ($50; $25k bond for out-of-state). Seller disclosure at sale: YES mandatory (Ch. 558A / 481 IAC 2014.1(7)) BUT no chimney/fireplace/flue line item (20-item form, lead line added 2026). Right to cancel a sale made at your home: YES (Ch. 555A). Carbon monoxide alarm law: YES — § 10A.518, fireplace-triggered, rentals + new construction since Jul 1 2018; no pre-sale certificate. Where to check a contractor: DIAL contractor search + dial.iowa.gov hearth license + iowaattorneygeneral.gov complaints. Then ask the eight questions below, get the inspection findings in writing with photos, and never sign for "emergency" work on the day of a door-knock.

faq.q: Is a chimney inspection required when a home sells in Iowa?
faq.a: Iowa mandates seller disclosure under Iowa Code Chapter 558A, but the state form does NOT name chimney, fireplace, or flue. - Delivery (§ 558A.2): the transferor or their broker must deliver a written disclosure statement before a written offer is made or accepted. - Content (§ 558A.4): statements cover property condition, including "significant defects in the structural integrity" and, since a 2025 amendment effective Jan 1, 2026, lead service lines. The Real Estate Commission sets the content by rule. - Where the rule lives now: the old 193E—14.1 rule was transferred to 481 IAC 2014.1 (IAC Supplement 6/10/26). The form is at subrule 2014.1(7) (history: ARC 0027D, effective 4/22/26). - What the form lists: the current form has 20 numbered items. Among them are Basement/Foundation, Roof, Heating System(s), Physical Problems and Structural Damage, plus a new item 13: "Are there currently, or have there ever been, any lead water service lines present?" None names chimney, fireplace, flue or wood stove.

faq.q: Can I cancel a chimney contract I signed at my door in Iowa?
faq.a: Iowa gives consumers two tracks, plus a cancellation right: - (1) Iowa Consumer Fraud Act, § 714.16. It bars deception, fraud, false promise, misrepresentation and concealment of material fact. The AG enforces it. - (2) Private right of action, Ch. 714H.
